{{short description|Swiss mathematician, teacher and peace activist (1891-1970)}}
[[File:Rosenblatt Stahelin Tonolo Zullig Zurich1932.tif|thumb|''Left to right:'' {{ill|Alfred Rosenblatt|es}}, [[Helene Stähelin (mathematician)|Helene Stähelin]] (in background), {{ill|Angelo Tonolo|it}}, and J. Züllig, at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], [[Zürich]] 1932]]
'''Helene Stähelin''' (18 July 1891 – 30 December 1970) was a Swiss mathematician, teacher, and peace activist.<ref name="Nipp.2014">{{cite web|title=Personenlexikon des Kanton Basel-Landschaft &mdash; Helene Stähelin|author=Manuela Nipp|url=https://personenlexikon.bl.ch/Helene_St%C3%A4helin|access-date=25 Jun 2017}}</ref> From 1948 to 1967, she was president of the Swiss section of the [[Women's International League for Peace and Freedom]] and its representative in the Swiss Peace Council.<ref name="Ludi.1998">{{cite web|title=No 12 &mdash; Stähelin, Helene | author=Regula Ludi|url=http://www.hls-dhs-dss.ch/textes/d/D21110.php|access-date=25 Jun 2017}}</ref><ref name="Willi.0000">{{cite web|title=Geschichte der WILPFSchweiz &mdash; Eine Bewegung entsteht|author=Irene Willi|url= http://www.wilpfschweiz.ch/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=34&Itemid=45 |access-date=25 Jun 2017}}</ref>

==Life==
Born in [[Wintersingen]], Stähelin was one of twelve children of the [[parson]] Gustav Stähelin (1858&ndash;1934)<ref>{{cite web|title="Online Catalogue of the State Archives Basel-Stadt &mdash; PA 182a B 55 Gustav Stähelin-Lieb (1858-1934), Pfr. § 113 bzw. 207 neu, s.d. (sine dato) (Serie)|url=https://query.staatsarchiv.bs.ch/query/detail.aspx?ID=421954|access-date=25 Jun 2017}}</ref> and his wife Luise ([[née]] Lieb). In 1894, the family moved from Wintersingen to [[Allschwil]]. Stähelin attended the Töchterschule in [[Basel]], the [[University of Basel]], and the [[University of Göttingen]]. 

In 1922, she became teacher of mathematics and natural sciences at the Töchterinstitut in [[Ftan]].<ref name="Nipp.2014" /> In 1924, she obtained her DPhil from Basel University.<ref name="query.staatsarchiv.bs.ch">{{cite web |title=Online Catalogue of the State Archives Basel-Stadt &mdash; PA 182a B 90 Helene Staehelin (1891-1971), Dr. phil. § 207,4 neu, 1955 (Serie) |url=https://query.staatsarchiv.bs.ch/query/detail.aspx?ID=422294 |access-date=25 Jun 2017}}</ref> Her dissertation was advised by [[Hans Mohrmann]] and {{ill|Otto Spiess|de}}.<ref name="Nipp.2014" /><ref>{{cite thesis | type=Ph.D. thesis | author=Helene Stähelin | title=Die charakteristischen Zahlen analytischer Kurven auf dem Kegel zweiter Ordnung und ihrer Studyschen Bildkurven | institution=Basel University | year=1924 }}
</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/download/PPN235181684_0093/PPN235181684_0093___LOG_0019.pdf | author=Helene Stähelin | title=Die charakteristischen Zahlen analytischer Kurven auf dem Kegel zweiter Ordnung und ihrer Studyschen Bildkurven | journal=[[Mathematische Annalen]] | volume=93  | pages=217–229 | year=1925 | doi=10.1007/BF01449961 | hdl=2027/mdp.39015069431917 | s2cid=118344883 }}</ref> In 1926, she became a member of the [[Swiss Mathematical Society]]. Between 1934 and 1956, Stähelin worked as teacher at the Protestant secondary school in [[Zug]]. After her pensioning she returned to Basel, where she assisted for several years in Otto Spiess' editing of the [[Bernoulli family]] letters.<ref name="Nipp.2014" /><ref>S. Gehr, F. Nagel, B. v. Reibnitz (Ed.), [https://www.margini.unibas.ch/web/resource/CatalogoBasel.pdf ''Editionen in Basel''], 2010, p.22-23 (20-21)</ref>

Being a [[pacifist]], Stähelin committed herself to the [[Women's International League for Peace and Freedom]] (IFFF) and its struggle against scientific warfare. She was president of the IFFF's Swiss section from 1947&ndash;1967, during which the main issues were the [[United Nations]], [[nuclear weapons]], and the [[Vietnam War]].<ref name="Nipp.2014" /> Due to her peace activism, she was watched by Swiss authorities in the mid 1950s;<ref name="Nipp.2014" /> her file at the {{ill|Swiss Public Prosecutor General|de|Schweizerische Bundesanwaltschaft}} was kept secret until 1986.<ref name="query.staatsarchiv.bs.ch" /> Stähelin advocated for [[women's suffrage in Switzerland]], though she died before women were able to vote.<ref name="Nipp.2014" /> She died in Basel.
